description:
Found by Elixir Parity for fz-mue.2; reproduced by fz-engine. Repros: /private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-j5n-Workspace-fz/b224cdcb-7600-490e-8ff8-226a23f89665/scratchpad/mue/ (m1 = smallest: a value/cont array decoder; m5, m6 self-recursive controls; k4-k6 small cycles).

Defect: once a fold has put a widened member (list(any)) into a standing type, a later ladder that is a subtype of that member is never seen as growth.
- Evidence site (World::fold_clashes_against_standing_row): a new contribution is compared with the joined column only. The joined column is correlation-blind, so a row that deepens one list level per analysis is "already covered", clash_fold exits at is_subtype(new, old), and the exact row is stored. m1 on fz-9zq.2: 2 activations, 6,777 AnalyzeActivation runs, 23,555 contributions to cont, then a stack overflow in types emptiness on a list nested thousands deep. On develop it exhausts the 50k budget earlier (the per-rung key ladder fz-9zq.2 removes).
- Return site (define_return -> clash_fold): Walk::slot unions slots across tuple clauses, so a growing clause's slot hides behind a widened clause's slot although the clause pairs it with a different sibling slot. Elixir Parity's unit probe: {list(L_k), :array|:ok|list(int)} at k vs k+1 folds at k=1,2,3 without a {list(any), ...} clause and never with it. The return then climbs to RETURN_WIDENING_BUDGET (11 revisions) and goes to any.

Spike (fz-engine, on fz-9zq.2's e4e99c859): fold each column against the joined column and, failing that, against that column of each standing row. m1, m5, m6, k4, k5, k6 all compile and print the right value. The return site is not yet changed and not yet shown to need it once the evidence site is fixed.

Owed before building: gate and pin census of the spike; whether the return-site pairing is still needed (the unit probe says the masking is real; decide whether it is fixed here or shown harmless); order-independence over 12 job orders; a fix-proposal page.
Stacks on fz-9zq.2 (the m1 fixture needs the cycle rule to get past the key ladder).
title: A contribution folds against each standing row, so a widened member cannot hide a ladder
